review.conclusion_reason: NO contradicts the unresolved paragraph (2) and missing proof of the statutory trigger. Under amendment_follows_parent, the supported operative result is OPEN: establish the first Administrator's taking office and a qualifying ending of the parent/amended provision. Formal status must separately record demonstrated partial supersession of paragraph (3) on 1934-04-19; whole-order revocation or supersession is not established. T4 is supported by the accepted original, complete clause inventory, verified paragraph (3) replacement, and specifically identified paragraph (2) gap, using the corrected OPEN conclusion; T5 is not.
missed_evidence: The TTB page's full sentence links its twenty-month narrative to enactment in August 1935; it supplies an approximate date but not the taking-office event required by section 10. This limits p11 rather than closing the gap.
review.stop_code_verdict: confirmed: WEB fits the first gap. The evidence slice identifies held originals and paragraph (3) replacements, but no record establishing when the first FAA Administrator took office. The separate legal-interpretation gap does not change this factual gap's code.
review.suspected_defect: The categorical NO and revoked_or_superseded conclusion appears substituted for OPEN despite the worker's own open clause and unresolved ending conditions. The verified successor orders supersede only paragraph (3).

verdicts.reason: Held GPO text expressly substitutes paragraphs (2) and (3); no other operative provision appears.
Held text confirms six presidential designees, one vote each, and an additional Director vote on a tie.
Held paragraph (3) contains the quoted appointment language and six names.
Held text expressly requires designation of an Assistant Director; OCR spacing does not obscure the command.
Held EO 6683 names EO 6576 and substitutes all of paragraph (3), dated April 19, 1934.
Both held successor texts contain only the six-member designation within substituted paragraph (3), omitting both Director-duty sentences. EO 6788 names both earlier amendments.
Held EO 6474 invokes NIRA title I and establishes FACA in paragraph (1).

49 Stat. 987, section 10, confirms abolition of the described agency without an executive-order number; effectiveness is conditional as p9 states. https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/STATUTE-49/pdf/STATUTE-49-Pg977.pdf, PDF page 11.
Section 10 expressly conditions effectiveness on the first Administrator taking office. Same PDF, page 11.

Chapter URL failed, but the identical 2021 title compilation confirms the quotation and both order numbers in the sections 209–210 Codification note: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2021-title27/html/USCODE-2021-title27.htm. It describes agency abolition, not express revocation of the orders.

The quotation is authentic, but 'without a date' omits the same sentence's attribution to signing the FAA Act in August 1935. That narrative does not establish the statutory taking-office event. https://www.ttb.gov/business-central/trade-practices/federal-alcohol-administration-act-historical-background
